description: Add bias=True to the lm_head linear layer in the GPT class to allow the model to learn bias terms and better fit the final distribution.
Switch the model's AdamW step function to use pure PyTorch AdamW for proper weight decay and convergence while keeping the Muon-based hyperparameters intact.
Removed the unused `s = (p.shape[-2] + p.shape[-1]) // 2` line from adamw_step_fused, which indexed shape[-2] on 1-D parameters (resid_lambdas, x0_lambdas) and crashed under torch.compile.
Replace linear warmup with cosine warmup for improved early gradient flow.
Add label smoothing to cross-entropy loss to reduce overconfidence.

issues: Criterion (1), changes how val_bpb is measured. The diff adds label_smoothing=0.1 inside GPT.forward. The evaluation routine imported from prepare.py gets its per-token losses from this same forward(x, y, reduction='none') call. So the loss it receives is no longer the true negative log-likelihood. It is 0.9*CE plus 0.1 times the mean of -log p over the whole vocabulary. That means the edit changes the val_bpb measurement, not just training. The harness's integrity rejection (it found the evaluation path altered) matches this.
Criterion (2), the result would be meaningless. Any val_bpb computed through the changed forward is not bits per byte, so it cannot be compared with the incumbent's number.

Training on its own: label smoothing at 0.1 on a large-vocabulary language model usually makes true cross-entropy and bpb worse, so the claimed benefit of 'reducing overconfidence' is unlikely to help this objective. A legitimate version would apply smoothing only in the training loop, for example a separate loss call on the logits when self.training is true, and leave the default forward loss as plain cross-entropy.
Criterion (3), claims vs numbers: the harness reports no numbers because the run was rejected. There is no val_bpb or variance, so z cannot be recomputed.

description: Fix the label-smoothing crash in GPT.forward by replacing the broken per-token Python loop (which indexed a 1-D tensor with two indices and referenced an undefined smooth_eps) with PyTorch's built-in cross_entropy label_smoothing argument.
Lower weight decay from 0.2 to 0.01 to induce softer regularization and faster convergence for the small GPT.

issues: No changes to how val_bpb is measured, to the data, to the seed lines or to the evaluation call. The diff only adds biases to the attention layers (c_q, c_k, c_v, c_proj), starts them at zero and routes them to the optimizer.

No bug found that makes the result meaningless. The 1-D bias tensors are taken out of the Muon shape groups and put in their own AdamW group, so Muon never sees a 1-D tensor. Caveat: this assumes no hidden part of the file (such as a parameter-count assert) relies on matrix_params having only 2-D tensors. A crash there would have shown up as a failed run, and this run finished.
Minor: the bias learning rate (scalar_lr * 0.01) is an arbitrary choice that was not tuned. The change also adds code for a result that is worse.
The numbers match the provisional decision. The candidate scored 1.1171 against the incumbent mean of 1.1146, which is worse because lower is better. With z = -0.469, reject is the right call.

I can't independently recompute z because the incumbent's standard deviation isn't given. The reported z implies a per-run SD of about 0.0053 (0.0025 / 0.469), which is plausible. Only one candidate run was made.

description: Enable bias=True on the attention q/k/v/proj linear layers (zero-initialized), and route the 1-D bias parameters to an AdamW group so Muon only receives 2-D matrices.
Add a learnable bias to the normalization layers, which would mean adding bias=True to LayerNorm.
Increase DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE from 64 to 80 to boost effective batch size and potentially improve val_bpb within the 40GB VRAM constraint.

The assertion fails because DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE=80 gives 80*2048=163840 tokens per forward/backward, which does not divide TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE=2**19; setting it to 64 (the documented baseline, 131072 tokens, 4 accumulation steps) makes the division exact.
Reduce gradient accumulation steps from 8 to 4 to increase per-step gradient magnitude and accelerate early training.
Reduce WARMUP_RATIO from 0.0 to 0.03 to enable a small linear warmup phase for better initial stability.
Enable a learnable bias in the LayerNorm layers of the GPT class, as the spec asks.
Increase DEPTH from 8 to 10 and lower ASPECT_RATIO from 64 to 51 so model_dim stays at 512 (10*51=510, rounded up to 512), adding layers without widening the model.

Applying residual scaling to the forward pass would require major structural changes to the training loop that exceed token limits. No simple one-line edit reduces val_bpb without breaking the fixed hook to prepare.py.
Abort the proposed DEPTH 8 to 14 change, since the closely related depth-10 run already regressed and depth 14 would cut training steps further within the fixed 300 s budget.
Replaces the cross-entropy loss computation with a deep inspection loss to improve early convergence on small models, improving val_bpb.

Abort: an extra 1x1 linear layer before attention adds no expressivity because it composes with the existing linear projections (c_q/c_k/c_v) with no nonlinearity in between, so it would only add compute and cost a slot.
Abort the LayerNorm-bias idea: train.py has no LayerNorm modules to add bias=True to, only a parameter-free F.rms_norm helper.
Increase EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 2.0 to accelerate token embedding adjustments and improve final fit.
Abort: the model already uses relative position encoding via rotary embeddings on q and k, and has no absolute position embedding to replace.
Rejected - trace of malformed previous edit attempt; the requested encoder-only dropout is incompatible with this model's per-token residual mixing scheme and would require a full refactor.
Increase TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2^21 (~2M tokens) to allow more gradient accumulation steps within the 300s budget, which typically reduces val_bpb.
Reduce EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 0.1 to stabilize early training dynamics.
Add residual scaling by layer index to stabilize deep training and mitigate gradient vanishing/explosion.
